messages:
alex: FYI ran a perfetto capture across a 10k request spike, there's a recurring 120-200ms gap in the client->gateway->runtime waterfall around the gateway handoff. link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/ABCD1234 :eyes:

marta: ugh, can you paste the waterfall snippet? is it at the gateway or at runtime kernel selection?

alex: pasted below (cropped):
```
client_send -> gateway_recv -> gateway_enqueue -> gateway_handoff  (120ms gap) -> runtime_pick_kernel -> runtime_kernel_launch -> runtime_kv_fetch
```
Looks like the handoff finishes but runtime_pick_kernel doesn't start for ~120ms sometimes.

devon: interesting — could be scheduling jitter on the gateway thread or a backpressure stall waiting for batch assembly. Any KV cache miss storms?

alex: KV miss rate spikes align with the gaps. The perfetto flame shows small CPU bursts then a long idle on the gateway worker thread. Also see multiple tiny kernel launches (<1ms) each separated by tens of ms.

jia: can we repro with nsys? nvtx around pick_kernel + kv_fetch + kernel_launch would help. Also collect thread names so we can see if the worker got preempted.

sam: added an ephemeral perf job: nsys capture on gateway+runtime under 5k/s load. grabbing nvprof later for GPU side.

perf-bot: scheduled capture job perf-2187-03 (nsys) on rgx-3 for 3m, notify #eng-runtime when available. :robot_face:

marta: quick hypothesis: the kernel selection path is doing a synchronous policy check that yields to the event loop when caches are cold. If the yield aligns with scheduling, we get the observed gap. Could reproduce by toggling the async_policy flag.

devon: good call. Try two toggles: 1) force synchronous selection (to see if it's the yield), 2) coalesce selection calls by adding a micro-batch window (5ms). Compare perfetto timelines and KV cache hit ratio.

alex: running three experiments now: control, force-sync, micro-batch-5ms. Will post perfetto links and a tiny trace diff.

(alex later): short results: force-sync reduced gaps but increased tail latency on heavy bursts (more contention). micro-batch-5ms reduced number of kernel launches by ~60% and flattened KV miss spikes; end-to-end P99 dropped from 450ms -> 290ms in this run. Perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/EFGH5678

marta: that's promising. micro-batch is cheaper but we need to check quality/regression on short queries. Also need to ensure cost model doesn't explode.

devon: next steps: run AB test with micro-batch=5ms on a replica fleet, run nsys sampling to ensure no GPU-side serialization introduced, and add NVTX around handshake to confirm kernel handshake fragmentation is fixed. I'll own nsys runs.

jia: also add a lightweight counter emit in gateway: `handshake_wait_ms` histogram to Sentry/metrics so we can alert if gaps reappear. simple patch: `metrics.hist("handshake_wait_ms").record(now - enqueued_at)`

sam: [tracked] created ticket INF-1843: micro-batch experiment + metrics + perf captures. attaching perfetto/nsys outputs when done.

alex: thanks all — I'll update the ticket with the control vs micro-batch perfetto diffs and a small script to reproduce locally (`tools/run_load.sh --rate 5k --trace perfetto --nvtx`).

marta: nice work. if micro-batch looks stable, let's make it opt-in on Dedicated first.

devon: FYI after initial nsys sample, kernel_launch stalls were due to frequent tiny kernel flips (quantized vs full kernels) — coalescing reduced kernel variant churn as well.

alex: noted, I'll include the kernel-variant churn numbers in INF-1843.

perf-bot: capture perf-2187-03 uploaded: https://perfetto.dev/trace/UPLOAD123, nsys dump at s3://redwood-perf/2187/nsys.tar.gz

marta: perfect. leaving this thread open for the AB results, closing once INF-1843 has rollout notes and regression checks. :white_check_mark:
